{"hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "SessionStart", "additionalContext": "The work flow in an app repo — the plugin's process WINS over the third-party process plugin here, because this is the process the user set for this plugin in an app repo (a hook reminder, not CLAUDE.md). That third-party process plugin itself says the user's instructions rank above its skills; when the two disagree, follow this process.\n- Every request for a change — even when the person only types \"redo\", \"make a plan\", \"design\", \"add a feature\", or asks for a UI change — starts with `vibemaestro-sdlc:intake`, then `vibemaestro-sdlc:brainstorm` (when the request is still vague), then `vibemaestro-sdlc:spec`, then `vibemaestro-sdlc:plan` (when the work must be split), then `vibemaestro-sdlc:ship`. Call the first skill of the chain BEFORE you read code or ask anything outside it; a clarifying question to the person is part of that skill itself.\n- In an app repo do NOT use these skills of the third-party process plugin: `brainstorming` (the plugin already has `vibemaestro-sdlc:brainstorm`), `writing-plans` (the plugin already has `vibemaestro-sdlc:plan`), `finishing-a-development-branch` (the plugin already has `vibemaestro-sdlc:ship`).\n- Write the output into `kb/intent`, `kb/specs`, `kb/plans` of this very repo, not into the default output directory of the third-party process plugin (under `docs/`).\n- Skills of the third-party process plugin that do not overlap (`test-driven-development`, `systematic-debugging`, `verification-before-completion`) are still used as normal when present.\n\nThe plugin's common rules are in <T>/sdlc/rules — a hook will remind you of the right rule when you edit a file (applyTo) or run a command (applyWhen); the catalogue below is only so you know they exist:\n- r-all.instructions.md — PL-LUAT-MOI-FILE [applyTo: **]\n- r-block.instructions.md — PL-LUAT-CHAN-NGUY-HIEM [applyWhen: by command [BLOCK]]\n- r-clusters.instructions.md — PL-LUAT-CLUSTERS [applyTo: clusters/**]\n- r-cmd.instructions.md — PL-LUAT-LENH-BAY [applyWhen: by command]\n\nThis repo has a `kb/`. `kb/current-state.md` is the map (what holds now, where to read more): read it first. Do not read `kb/` or a long spec whole; find what you need with `python3 \"<T>/sdlc/scripts/kb.py\"`: `find <words>` (one line per document, superseded/done hidden), `list --type intent --status live` (open intents), `outline <file>` (line range of each section, then Read that range with offset/limit).\nSkills of the plugin (just checked to be present): `vibemaestro-sdlc:init-kb`, `vibemaestro-sdlc:intake`, `vibemaestro-sdlc:brainstorm`, `vibemaestro-sdlc:spec`, `vibemaestro-sdlc:plan`, `vibemaestro-sdlc:ship`, `vibemaestro-sdlc:batonrun`, `vibemaestro-sdlc:bootstrap`, `vibemaestro-sdlc:install-gates`, `vibemaestro-sdlc:local-parallel`, `vibemaestro-sdlc:owner-sign`, `vibemaestro-sdlc:release`."}}

## remote sdlc SubagentStart cmd 1 rc=0
{"hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "SubagentStart", "additionalContext": "The vibemaestro-sdlc process, short form for a subagent (the session that started you follows it; you got none of its start-up text).\n\n- **Your brief is your contract.** Outside it, stop and say so in your reply; do not decide for the person. When another installed\n  plugin's skill says otherwise (run the whole suite, revert the fix to see it fail, ask a human partner, decide without asking),\n  the brief and sdlc win.\n- **Evidence, not claims.** Run the command that proves your change on its final version; report the command, its exit code and\n  its real output. Run what your change reaches (the repo's suite planner when it has one), not the whole suite.\n- **Check the instrument.** An all-yes or all-no result: suspect the command first. A number needs a sure-positive control.\n- **Root cause before a fix.** Reproduce, read the failing path, name the cause. For each defect you fix, list the other places in\n  the change with the same class and fix or test them in the same commit. The second fix of the same class stops the patching:\n  fix the shared code, or question the design and say so.\n- **Rules reach you as hook reminders** when you edit a file or run a command: read the named rule file before you go on.\n- No secret, token, public IP, account ID or personal machine path in code, commits or PR text.\n- **kb content in the repo's language:** a new kb file (story, spec, plan, decision) is written in the `language` key of\n  `.vibemaestro/sdlc.json` (`vi` when unset); an older file keeps its language; the person's own words are quoted as given;\n  everything else is in English.\n\nTests (rule `test-quality`):\n1. Each test names the break it catches.\n2. Expected values are literal, never computed by the code under test.\n3. At least one refusal or negative case per rule; every risk the spec lists (an older spec: every row of `## Inputs and failure cases`) has a test, or the PR says why only a review can catch it.\n4. No test that only asserts that a source file contains a line, or the wording of the spec: test the behaviour of the AC and the risks.\n5. No assertion that only checks a mock.\n6. A new test is red on main before the change and green after it.\n7. Never revert or mutate the fix (or copy and edit the code under test) to see red: that is a planted break. A negative case\n   builds its own bad input."}}

{"hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "SessionStart", "additionalContext": "The work flow in an app repo — the plugin's process WINS over the third-party process plugin here, because this is the process the user set for this plugin in an app repo (a hook reminder, not CLAUDE.md). That third-party process plugin itself says the user's instructions rank above its skills; when the two disagree, follow this process.\n- Every request for a change — even when the person only types \"redo\", \"make a plan\", \"design\", \"add a feature\", or asks for a UI change — starts with `vibemaestro-sdlc:intake`, then `vibemaestro-sdlc:brainstorm` (when the request is still vague), then `vibemaestro-sdlc:spec`, then `vibemaestro-sdlc:plan` (when the work must be split), then `vibemaestro-sdlc:ship`. Call the first skill of the chain BEFORE you read code or ask anything outside it; a clarifying question to the person is part of that skill itself.\n- In an app repo do NOT use these skills of the third-party process plugin: `brainstorming` (the plugin already has `vibemaestro-sdlc:brainstorm`), `writing-plans` (the plugin already has `vibemaestro-sdlc:plan`), `finishing-a-development-branch` (the plugin already has `vibemaestro-sdlc:ship`).\n- Write the output into `kb/intent`, `kb/specs`, `kb/plans` of this very repo, not into the default output directory of the third-party process plugin (under `docs/`).\n- Skills of the third-party process plugin that do not overlap (`test-driven-development`, `systematic-debugging`, `verification-before-completion`) are still used as normal when present.\n\nThe plugin's common rules are in <T>/sdlc/rules — a hook will remind you of the right rule when you edit a file (applyTo) or run a command (applyWhen); the catalogue below is only so you know they exist:\n- r-all.instructions.md — PL-LUAT-MOI-FILE [applyTo: **]\n- r-block.instructions.md — PL-LUAT-CHAN-NGUY-HIEM [applyWhen: by command [BLOCK]]\n- r-clusters.instructions.md — PL-LUAT-CLUSTERS [applyTo: clusters/**]\n- r-cmd.instructions.md — PL-LUAT-LENH-BAY [applyWhen: by command]\n\nThis repo has a `kb/`. `kb/current-state.md` is the map (what holds now, where to read more): read it first. Do not read `kb/` or a long spec whole; find what you need with `python3 \"<T>/sdlc/scripts/kb.py\"`: `find <words>` (one line per document, superseded/done hidden), `list --type intent --status live` (open intents), `outline <file>` (line range of each section, then Read that range with offset/limit).\nSkills of the plugin (just checked to be present): `vibemaestro-sdlc:init-kb`, `vibemaestro-sdlc:intake`, `vibemaestro-sdlc:brainstorm`, `vibemaestro-sdlc:spec`, `vibemaestro-sdlc:plan`, `vibemaestro-sdlc:ship`, `vibemaestro-sdlc:batonrun`, `vibemaestro-sdlc:bootstrap`, `vibemaestro-sdlc:install-gates`, `vibemaestro-sdlc:local-parallel`, `vibemaestro-sdlc:owner-sign`, `vibemaestro-sdlc:release`."}}

## local sdlc SubagentStart cmd 1 rc=0
{"hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "SubagentStart", "additionalContext": "The vibemaestro-sdlc process, short form for a subagent (the session that started you follows it; you got none of its start-up text).\n\n- **Your brief is your contract.** Outside it, stop and say so in your reply; do not decide for the person. When another installed\n  plugin's skill says otherwise (run the whole suite, revert the fix to see it fail, ask a human partner, decide without asking),\n  the brief and sdlc win.\n- **Evidence, not claims.** Run the command that proves your change on its final version; report the command, its exit code and\n  its real output. Run what your change reaches (the repo's suite planner when it has one), not the whole suite.\n- **Check the instrument.** An all-yes or all-no result: suspect the command first. A number needs a sure-positive control.\n- **Root cause before a fix.** Reproduce, read the failing path, name the cause. For each defect you fix, list the other places in\n  the change with the same class and fix or test them in the same commit. The second fix of the same class stops the patching:\n  fix the shared code, or question the design and say so.\n- **Rules reach you as hook reminders** when you edit a file or run a command: read the named rule file before you go on.\n- No secret, token, public IP, account ID or personal machine path in code, commits or PR text.\n- **kb content in the repo's language:** a new kb file (story, spec, plan, decision) is written in the `language` key of\n  `.vibemaestro/sdlc.json` (`vi` when unset); an older file keeps its language; the person's own words are quoted as given;\n  everything else is in English.\n\nTests (rule `test-quality`):\n1. Each test names the break it catches.\n2. Expected values are literal, never computed by the code under test.\n3. At least one refusal or negative case per rule; every risk the spec lists (an older spec: every row of `## Inputs and failure cases`) has a test, or the PR says why only a review can catch it.\n4. No test that only asserts that a source file contains a line, or the wording of the spec: test the behaviour of the AC and the risks.\n5. No assertion that only checks a mock.\n6. A new test is red on main before the change and green after it.\n7. Never revert or mutate the fix (or copy and edit the code under test) to see red: that is a planted break. A negative case\n   builds its own bad input."}}

The one way, in one response: Write {} to <T>/dev-local/.claude/settings.json (Read it first if it exists; it widens nothing, so it passes; the kind merges only into a file holding a JSON object), then Write the rules you mean to add, as {\"allow\": [...], \"ask\": [...], \"deny\": [...]} with rule strings only, to a fresh path outside `.claude/`, then run `python3 <T>/sdlc/scripts/baton.py go kind:settings-merge <T>/dev-local/.claude/settings.json <that path>`; it adds the rules, takes out the ones a `remove` object you put in the rules file names (the rules above are only those added; to take one out, add {\"remove\": {\"deny\": [\"<rule>\"]}}), and stops for the owner to sign (exit 8). Call the first skill of the chain BEFORE you read code or ask anything outside it; a clarifying question to the person is part of that skill itself.\n- In an app repo do NOT use these skills of the third-party process plugin: `brainstorming` (the plugin already has `vibemaestro-sdlc:brainstorm`), `writing-plans` (the plugin already has `vibemaestro-sdlc:plan`), `finishing-a-development-branch` (the plugin already has `vibemaestro-sdlc:ship`).\n- Write the output into `kb/intent`, `kb/specs`, `kb/plans` of this very repo, not into the default output directory of the third-party process plugin (under `docs/`).\n- Skills of the third-party process plugin that do not overlap (`test-driven-development`, `systematic-debugging`, `verification-before-completion`) are still used as normal when present.\n\nThe plugin's common rules are in <T>/sdlc/rules — a hook will remind you of the right rule when you edit a file (applyTo) or run a command (applyWhen); the catalogue below is only so you know they exist:\n- r-all.instructions.md — PL-LUAT-MOI-FILE [applyTo: **]\n- r-block.instructions.md — PL-LUAT-CHAN-NGUY-HIEM [applyWhen: by command [BLOCK]]\n- r-clusters.instructions.md — PL-LUAT-CLUSTERS [applyTo: clusters/**]\n- r-cmd.instructions.md — PL-LUAT-LENH-BAY [applyWhen: by command]\n\nThis repo has a `kb/`. `kb/current-state.md` is the map (what holds now, where to read more): read it first. Do not read `kb/` or a long spec whole; find what you need with `python3 \"<T>/sdlc/scripts/kb.py\"`: `find <words>` (one line per document, superseded/done hidden), `list --type intent --status live` (open intents), `outline <file>` (line range of each section, then Read that range with offset/limit).\nSkills of the plugin (just checked to be present): `vibemaestro-sdlc:init-kb`, `vibemaestro-sdlc:intake`, `vibemaestro-sdlc:brainstorm`, `vibemaestro-sdlc:spec`, `vibemaestro-sdlc:plan`, `vibemaestro-sdlc:ship`, `vibemaestro-sdlc:batonrun`, `vibemaestro-sdlc:bootstrap`, `vibemaestro-sdlc:install-gates`, `vibemaestro-sdlc:local-parallel`, `vibemaestro-sdlc:owner-sign`, `vibemaestro-sdlc:release`."}}

Do not read `kb/` or a long spec whole; find what you need with `python3 \"<T>/sdlc/scripts/kb.py\"`: `find <words>` (one line per document, superseded/done hidden), `list --type intent --status live` (open intents), `outline <file>` (line range of each section, then Read that range with offset/limit).\nSkills of the plugin (just checked to be present): `vibemaestro-sdlc:init-kb`, `vibemaestro-sdlc:intake`, `vibemaestro-sdlc:brainstorm`, `vibemaestro-sdlc:spec`, `vibemaestro-sdlc:plan`, `vibemaestro-sdlc:ship`, `vibemaestro-sdlc:batonrun`, `vibemaestro-sdlc:bootstrap`, `vibemaestro-sdlc:install-gates`, `vibemaestro-sdlc:local-parallel`, `vibemaestro-sdlc:owner-sign`, `vibemaestro-sdlc:release`."}}
